current.text: Mark Williams is out long term with a torn labrum. Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach have both started at center in preseason, with similar minutes, and the center minutes could be split.
He is projected as the opening night starting center, but with little confidence. The expert doubts he will get starter-level minutes.
He put up big numbers at the end of last season while Williams had a foot issue. In 24 starts he averaged 27 minutes, 8.6 rebounds and 3 assists on 67% shooting.
He is a last-pick option at best with little upside. He would need about 29 minutes a night to be worth getting excited about.
Phoenix has the best fantasy schedule in the league: 4 games in each of the playoff weeks 19 to 21, plus the fewest back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is a low-usage big and a smart passer. His fantasy value comes from FG% and assists, plus a few rebounds and steals. One expert calls him a tall TJ McConnell.
He has no shooting range beyond five feet and makes no threes. He can put the ball on the floor.
He is a very poor free throw shooter, under 50% from the line.
He is a very underrated defender.
His very low usage makes him a poor fantasy player unless he gets heavy minutes.

note: Both sites price him at 0 to 1 USD (Yahoo rank 170, ESPN rank 125), so he is likely outside our 144 drafted players and should not cost more than 1 USD as a last pick. If his minutes reach about 29, his starter line from last season (8.6 rebounds, 3 assists, 67% shooting) could help a punt FT% build that wants FG% and assists from a center. Watch the Maluach split in the first two weeks, and note that PHX's 4-4-4 playoff schedule adds a little late-season value.
